openObservations.title: Controlled route recovery is needed when current-action routing is wrong or blocks validation
openObservations.sourceArtifact: Operator discussion after WC08-REPAIR02 validation was blocked by incorrect routing to WC09 Ad Hoc Work Card Capture.
openObservations.operatorObservation: The Operator needs a controlled recovery path when current-action routing is wrong, has advanced too far, is stuck on stale state, or prevents access to the validation/review screen needed to continue. The app should not trap the Operator behind a broken route, but it also should not let the Operator casually mark work complete, skip validation, or advance phases without evidence.
openObservations.architectDisposition: Assigned to immediate repair after WC08-REPAIR01 validation confirmed the non-mutating prompt-style route guidance is insufficient for an end-user product workflow.
openObservations.dispositionRationale: The app must provide a controlled in-application recovery path when routing is wrong, stale, or blocks validation. The recovery path must be governed by durable evidence and Architect disposition, not an unrestricted Operator override and not a copy/paste prompt to an Architect or LLM.
openObservations.assignedTarget: WC08-REPAIR04 — Controlled Route Recovery and Accurate Route Evidence Authority

openObservations.title: Artifact authority and revision governance is undefined
openObservations.sourceArtifact: Architect review of amended WC08-REPAIR02 Human Validation Reports and duplicate _2 validation artifacts created by the application.
openObservations.architectObservation: The application creates a new suffixed validation artifact when an existing report is amended instead of updating, superseding, or explicitly identifying one authoritative revision. Multiple durable reports can therefore represent the same workflow event.
openObservations.architectDisposition: Promote to project-level architectural governance and require explicit design before implementation.
openObservations.dispositionRationale: Artifact identity and artifact revision are separate concepts. Every workflow artifact must have exactly one authoritative revision, and authority must not be inferred from filename suffixes, filesystem ordering, creation timestamps, or directory enumeration.
openObservations.architecturalDetermination: ChampCity A/I shall distinguish artifact identity from artifact revision. One artifact represents one durable workflow event; revisions represent edits. The workflow model must explicitly resolve exactly one authoritative revision for all durable workflow artifact types.
candidateImplementationModels: Single authoritative artifact with overwrite semantics and Git history
Explicitly versioned artifacts with superseded metadata
Immutable artifacts with a separate authoritative index
openObservations.assignedTarget: Future artifact authority and revision governance Work Card before workflow automation depends on duplicate or revised artifacts.
